title: ASTRA: Automatic Sizing of Transistors with Reasoning Agents
problem: Advancing technology nodes have increased transistor sizing complexity in analog circuit design. Existing AI techniques lack integrated domain expertise, resulting in slow convergence and inefficient optimization.
motivation: Analog circuit design automation is critical for modern IC development, but existing AI approaches are purely data-driven without access to domain knowledge like gm/ID methodology.
method: Proposes ASTRA, an optimization framework implementing Model Context Protocol (MCP) to create structured reasoning pathways between LLMs, domain knowledge bases, and Bayesian Optimization. Two-stage process: (1) MCP-guided design initialization leveraging RAG to identify feasible regions using gm/ID methodology, and (2) BO-based optimization targeting critical transistors identified through LLM reasoning with data-driven validation. Seamlessly integrates with existing transistor sizing algorithms.
key_novelty: First LLM-assisted transistor sizing framework combining domain knowledge, reasoning agents, and Bayesian optimization, achieving up to 4.35× fewer simulation iterations.
contributions: MCP-based integration of LLMs with domain knowledge bases for circuit design
RAG-driven design initialization using gm/ID methodology
LLM-guided critical transistor identification with BO-based optimization
Up to 4.35× fewer simulations and 2.36× performance improvements on real circuits
Open-source framework compatible with multiple sizing algorithms
limitations: Evaluation on three analog circuits; generalization to different circuit types not thoroughly explored; LLM hallucination potential not fully addressed.
